Need to search first.I don't have any notes for you this time. None of my research worked, and I've hit the limit on tool calls for this session, so I couldn't read a single source page.

The first set of page requests (Enduring Word, Bible Hub, Precept Austin, GotQuestions and the NET Bible) was rejected. The tool will only open a page after it has turned up in a search first. I then ran the searches to get those links, but by then I'd used up my tool calls and nothing came back.

Because your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, I haven't written any verse notes from memory or guessed at links.

**If you'd like me to try again** (in a new message or session), I'd do it in this order:
1. Search first, then open the verse-by-verse pages for the traditional reading: Enduring Word on Ezekiel 39, Bible Hub's commentary pages for Ezekiel 39 (Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and others), Precept Austin and Wesley's notes on StudyLight.
2. Cover the points where Protestant traditions differ, mainly:
   - who Gog and Magog are;
   - when the battle happens, before or after the millennium (compare Revelation 20:8);
   - whether the seven years and seven months are literal (vv. 9–16);
   - how the feast for the birds (vv. 17–20) relates to Revelation 19:17–18;
   - how the outpouring of the Spirit in v. 29 relates to Pentecost.
   
   For these I'd use GotQuestions, Desiring God, Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition, Sam Storms and the AG site.
3. For other views, read the NET Bible notes on Ezekiel 39, any Bible Odyssey article on Gog, and the Catholic Encyclopedia (New Advent) and Catholic.com on Gog and Magog.

You could also paste the links or text of any pages you'd like me to work from. Then I can write the verse-by-verse notes, citing only those pages.
